'''Sumner Byron Myers''' (February 19, 1910 – October 8, 1955) was an American [[mathematician]] specializing in [[topology]] and [[differential geometry]]. He studied at [[Harvard University]] under [[Marston Morse|H. C. Marston Morse]],<ref name="inter">[[Albert W. Tucker|Tucker, A]]: ''[http://www.princeton.edu/~mudd/finding_aids/mathoral/pmc33.htm Interview with Albert Tucker] {{webarchive| url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121008032725/http://www.princeton.edu/~mudd/finding_aids/mathoral/pmc33.htm |date=2012-10-08 }}'', Princeton University, July 11, 1984. Last accessed January 1, 2010.</ref> where he graduated with a [[Ph.D.]] in 1932.<ref name="grad">Mathematics Genealogy Project: ''[http://genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/html/id.phtml?id=7746 Sumner Byron Myers]'', no date. Last accessed December 5, 2005.</ref> Myers then pursued postdoctoral studies at [[Princeton University]] (1934–1936)<ref name="members">Princeton University: ''[http://www.math.ias.edu/mnames.html Members of the School of Mathematics] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20001213114100/http://www.math.ias.edu/mnames.html |date=2000-12-13 }}'', no date. Last accessed December 5, 2005.</ref> before becoming a professor for mathematics at the [[University of Michigan]]. He died unexpectedly from a heart attack during the [[1955 Michigan Wolverines football team|1955 Michigan–Army]] football game at [[Michigan Stadium]].<ref>{{cite book |title=The Michigan Alumnus |volume=62 |publisher=UM Libraries |year=1955 |page=90 |url={{Google books |plainurl=yes |id=tQTiAAAAMAAJ |page=90 }} }}</ref>

==Sumner B. Myers Prize==
The Sumner B. Myers Prize was created in his honor for distinguished theses within the [[College of Literature, Science, and the Arts|LSA]] Mathematics Department.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://lsa.umich.edu/math/graduates/StudentAwards/department-awards.html |title=Department Awards |author= <!--Not stated--> |website= LSA Mathematics |publisher= University of Michigan |access-date= 29 August 2022 |quote= |language= }}</ref><ref name="award">University of Michigan: ''[http://www.math.lsa.umich.edu/undergrad/Sumner%20Myers.pdf Sumner Myers Award]'', no date. Last accessed December 5, 2005.</ref> Notable recipients include [[June Huh]], [[Mary Wootters]], and [[Theodore J. Kaczynski]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Department Awards {{!}} U-M LSA Mathematics |url=https://lsa.umich.edu/math/graduates/StudentAwards/department-awards.html |access-date=2024-06-03 |website=lsa.umich.edu |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Mary Wootters named the recipient of the 2022 James L. Massey Award {{!}} IEEE Information Theory Society |url=https://www.itsoc.org/news/mary-wootters-named-recipient-2022-james-l-massey-award |access-date=2024-06-03 |website=www.itsoc.org}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=McFadden |first=Robert D. |date=1996-05-26 |title=PRISONER OF RAGE -- A special report.;From a Child of Promise to the Unabom Suspect |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1996/05/26/us/prisoner-of-rage-a-special-report-from-a-child-of-promise-to-the-unabom-suspect.html |access-date=2024-06-03 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref>
